blocks.text: Chemical manufacturing relies on two main pillars: reaction engineering and separation technology. Several key chemical processes are used in industrial production; some of them are:

Small molecules called monomers link up to form large chains called polymers. In addition polymerisation, monomers add to one another without losing any atoms (for example ethene monomers forming poly(ethene)). In condensation polymerisation, monomers join and release a small molecule, usually water (for example monomers forming polyesters). Engro Polymer and Chemicals is the only producer of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) in Pakistan.

In refining, fractional distillation separates crude oil into products by their boiling points; the most important fractions include gasoline, diesel and kerosene. Reforming converts straight-chain hydrocarbons into branched ones to improve fuel quality; in catalytic reforming, hydrocarbons are heated with a catalyst to give high-octane gasoline. Cracking and reforming at refineries such as PARCO and Attock Refinery provide essential petrochemical feedstocks for the wider chemical industry.

Ammonia (NH3) is made from nitrogen (N2) and hydrogen (H2), with iron as the catalyst: N2 + 3H2 <=> 2NH3. This process accounts for 13% of the nitrogen fixation on Earth, and 70% of the ammonia is used directly to make fertilisers. Large plants such as Engro Fertilizers and FFC use natural gas as the feedstock to produce ammonia, which is then converted into urea.

Sulphur dioxide is converted into sulphur trioxide using V2O5 or platinum as the catalyst: 2SO2 + O2 <=> 2SO3. The SO3 is absorbed to form oleum, which is then converted into sulphuric acid: SO3 + H2SO4 -> H2S2O7, then H2S2O7 + H2O -> 2H2SO4. The process gives highly pure, concentrated H2SO4. Sulphuric acid is the most used chemical in the world, so it is often called the 'king of chemicals'. In Pakistan several plants, for example Nimir Industrial Chemicals, run the contact process.

The Solvay process makes sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) from brine and limestone. Ammonia is added to brine and carbon dioxide is passed through it, forming a precipitate of sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO3): NaCl + NH3 + CO2 + H2O -> NaHCO3 + NH4Cl. Heating converts it into sodium carbonate: 2NaHCO3 -> Na2CO3 + CO2 + H2O. Ammonia is regenerated using lime from the decomposition of calcium carbonate (CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2; CaO + 2NH4Cl -> CaCl2 + 2NH3 + H2O), and the by-product is calcium chloride (CaCl2). Lucky Core Industries (formerly ICI) produces soda ash for the glass, detergent and paper industries.

The chlor-alkali process is an industrial electrolysis of sodium chloride brine that gives three key products: chlorine (Cl2), sodium hydroxide (NaOH, caustic soda) and hydrogen (H2): 2NaCl + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + Cl2 + H2. It is crucial for making plastics, detergents and water-treatment products, and it commonly uses modern membrane-cell technology for high efficiency and purity. Sitara Chemical Industries and Ittehad Chemicals are leading producers in Pakistan, supporting the textile and water-treatment sectors.
